The Fathers continue to constitute an indispensable point of reference for Christian life today.

Profound and authoritative witnesses of the most immediate apostolic tradition, direct participants in the life of Christian communities, a very rich pastoral theme stands out in them, a development of dogma illuminated by a special charisma, an understanding of the Scriptures that has the Spirit as its guide.

The penetration of the Christian message into the socio-cultural environment of their time, by imposing the examination of various problems, each more delicate, leads the Fathers to indicate solutions that prove to be extraordinarily current for us.

Hence the "return to the Fathers" through an editorial initiative that tries to detect the most vivid and sometimes also the most painful demands in which the Christian community of our time is struggling, to clarify them in the light of the approaches and solutions that the Fathers provide to their communities. This can also be a guarantee of certainty at a time when poorly understood forms of pluralism can cause doubts and uncertainties when facing vital problems.

The collection, prepared by the Ciudad Nueva Publishing House, with the advice of Professor Quacquarelli, professor of Ancient Christian Literature at the University of Rome, is being produced by competent and specialized professors in each of the works, who translate into plain and modern prose the spontaneity with which the Fathers wrote.

The Oratio catechetica magna by Gregory of Nyssa, written around the year 386, which now appears in the Spanish language, is one of the most exact syntheses of the Christian dogmatics of the first centuries. It has its own originality. While the other syntheses of this type (leaving aside the De catechizandis rudibus, of Saint Augustine) were directed, in most cases, to the teaching of catechumens in the main truths of the faith, with a view to Baptism, and were addressed directly to the initiates and the faithful to instruct them in the foundations of evangelical doctrine, the Oratio catechetica magna is addressed to the "leaders ecclesiastics", to the teachers or "catechists", who in the Church had the mission of promoting in believers an adequate formation on the doctrinal heritage of the apostolic tradition, taking into account the heretical tendencies within Christianity and the difficulties that came from the pagan or Jewish environment. Gregory weaves a masterful theological synthesis adapted to the fundamental instances of his time, responding, without the slightest polemical tone, to the objections made to the Christian faith. Thus, he deals with the great themes of dogmatics: the Trinitarian mystery, the creation of man, the origin and nature of evil, the Incarnation of the Word, the redemption of man, the sacraments of Baptism and the Eucharist, the need for faith and interior conversion, to conclude with the ultimate ends of man. Gregory's dogmatic exposition is animated by a dialogic posture, which connects with time and life, and framed within the arc of salvation history, which has as its driving center the Person and the redemptive work of Christ.
The agile and lively translation—due to the competence and good work of Professor Argimiro Velasco, Dominican, professor of patrology—is on par with the text, preserving its classic flavor.
